articles.title: India Bans Export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass With Immediate Effect
articles.excerpt: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade has changed the export status of lithium-ion battery black mass from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' with immediate effect, keeping the mineral-rich recycling material at home for India's battery and electric-vehicle supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Lithium-ion battery packs move along a production line. India has prohibited the export of lithium-ion battery black mass with immediate effect to keep the material for domestic processing.
articles.nri_angle: Keeping black mass at home affects the cost and availability of batteries across India's EV supply chain, which diaspora readers follow through India's auto and clean-energy industries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Losses More Than Double to Rs 22,238 Crore as Expansion Plan Meets Its Bill
articles.excerpt: Air India and Air India Express lost Rs 22,238 crore in the year ended March 2026, up from Rs 10,859 crore a year earlier, even as new CEO Tewolde Gebremariam seeks more widebody aircraft and Tata Sons weighs a capital infusion of more than Rs 10,000 crore.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora travellers, Air India's hub plans for Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru and the pace of its widebody expansion shape the nonstop options between India and North America and Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 62,370 Crore Fertiliser Subsidy for Rabi Season, DAP Price Held
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet has approved Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for Rabi 2026-27 with a tentative outlay of Rs 62,370.02 crore, up nearly 64% on the previous Rabi season, while holding the retail price of a 50 kg DAP bag at Rs 1,350.
articles.image_caption: A farmer broadcasts fertiliser by hand over a green field. The Cabinet has approved Rs 62,370 crore in P&K fertiliser subsidy for Rabi 2026-27 while holding the DAP bag price at Rs 1,350.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with farming families in India, the held DAP price of Rs 1,350 per 50 kg bag is the figure that reaches the farm gate this Rabi season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CPCB Says Diwali Data Gaps Came From Older Monitors' 1,000-Microgram Ceiling
articles.excerpt: In an 11-point clarification issued Tuesday, the Central Pollution Control Board said hourly readings above the calibrated range of its older particulate analysers were automatically treated as errors and dropped from Delhi's averages — and rejected allegations of under-reporting.
articles.image_caption: CPCB
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family in Delhi, the clarification explains why official AQI figures relatives rely on for health decisions can fall silent precisely when the air is at its worst.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BJP Wins 77 Tripura Civic Seats Unopposed as Opposition Alleges Intimidation
articles.excerpt: The State Election Commission declared 77 BJP candidates elected unopposed after the withdrawal of nominations closed, leaving 268 of the state's 345 urban local body seats to be contested on November 27.
articles.image_caption: Tripura
articles.nri_angle: Tripura's civic outcome shapes local governance in a state many diaspora families hail from, and the unopposed wins will frame the fairness debate around the November 27 vote.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hijack Threat Note Grounds Kolkata-Mumbai Air India Flight Before Takeoff
articles.excerpt: A threat found in the aircraft's washroom warning that the plane would be hijacked at 11:10 a.m. led officials to deboard all passengers and move the Mumbai-bound flight to an isolation bay at Kolkata airport on Wednesday morning.
articles.image_caption: Air India
articles.nri_angle: Kolkata-Mumbai is a busy domestic trunk route used by international passengers connecting through both hubs, so Wednesday's disruption affects onward travel plans well beyond the one flight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Hits 98.4% Immunisation Coverage, Yet Gaps Leave Millions Missing Shots
articles.excerpt: Full coverage rose from 62% in 2015 to 98.4% in January 2026 and zero-dose children nearly halved, but migration, hesitation, regional gaps and low adult uptake still leave many unprotected.
articles.image_caption: Immunisation
articles.nri_angle: Explains for diaspora families why a portable record such as U-WIN matters when children move between cities or countries, even as India's headline coverage reaches 98.4%.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IMD Forecasts Heavy Rain, Snow Till Nov 16 as Delhi AQI Eases to Poor
articles.excerpt: A Western Disturbance brings snow to the Western Himalayas till November 13, heavy rain returns to Tamil Nadu and Kerala on November 15-16, and Delhi records a 24-hour average AQI of 299 with no rain forecast till November 15.
articles.image_caption: Heavy
articles.nri_angle: Lets diaspora readers track the forecast for family districts — snow in Kashmir around Nov 12-13, heavy rain in Tamil Nadu and Kerala on Nov 15-16, and no rain for Delhi till Nov 15.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FICCI Puts Air Pollution's Annual Cost at $95 Billion, Urges Health-Led Plan
articles.excerpt: A FICCI-EY paper links polluted air to more than two million deaths in India in 2023 and calls for explicit PM2.5 targets, regional airshed action and year-round health planning instead of seasonal emergency responses.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of air pollution over northern India (NESDIS). A FICCI report put air pollution's annual cost to India at $95 billion and urged a health-led plan.
articles.nri_angle: Pollution on this scale shapes winter travel, family health and caregiving decisions for diaspora readers with parents and children in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Workers Die After Inhaling Toxic Gas at Tata's Hosur iPhone Plant
articles.excerpt: The contract workers were cleaning a nano-filtration tank at the Hosur plant's effluent treatment plant late on Monday. Apple, Tata Electronics and Tamil Nadu authorities will investigate, as officials say proper safety measures were not in place.
articles.nri_angle: The Hosur plant is a key node in Apple's India iPhone supply chain, which Tata now anchors with roughly 40 percent of Indian iPhone assembly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai Doctors Warn Oral Cancer Is Striking Patients in Their Late 20s
articles.excerpt: Jaslok's Dr Mehul Bansali links the younger cases to tobacco and gutkha habits beginning at 12-15 — and gives the 2-3 week rule for a mouth ulcer that will not heal.
articles.nri_angle: The actionable rule travels: a mouth ulcer that has not healed in 2-3 weeks needs a specialist and a biopsy decision, wherever you live — early-stage oral cancer is far more survivable than late-stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doctors List Early Lung Cancer Warning Signs People Keep Overlooking
articles.excerpt: A cough past three weeks, blood in sputum, repeated chest infections and unexplained weight loss should be checked, not waited out, oncologists and pulmonologists say.
articles.image_caption: Lung
articles.nri_angle: US-based readers get the exact CDC low-dose CT screening criteria — age 50 to 80 and a 20 pack-year smoking history — alongside the symptom thresholds Indian specialists cite.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Surprised We Are Still Alive': AIIMS Doctor Warns Delhi Air Is Poisonous
articles.excerpt: AIIMS professor Vijay Hadda says even healthy colleagues cannot shake throat irritation from Delhi's post-Diwali air, and that green crackers cut emissions by only about 30 per cent.
articles.image_caption: Traffic moves through dense smog near India Gate in New Delhi as air quality stays in the severe range. AIIMS pulmonary specialist Dr Vijay Hadda warned that even healthy young adults are reporting symptoms within hours of exposure.
articles.nri_angle: The warning matters to diaspora families with parents and relatives in Delhi deciding how much time outdoors is safe while AQI stays severe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chennai Air Worsens Sharply on Diwali as Four Areas Cross AQI 300
articles.excerpt: Valasaravakkam hit 343 and the CPCB city average rose to 199 from 142 a year earlier — the steepest rise among major cities — despite a two-window firecracker rule that was widely ignored.
articles.image_caption: Fireworks burst over a haze-covered street during Diwali celebrations in Chennai. The city's average AQI rose to 199 from 142 a year earlier, and four neighbourhoods crossed 300 into the very poor band.
articles.nri_angle: Chennai is a top origin and destination city for diaspora travel during the festival season, and post-Diwali air quality shapes return-trip health planning for visiting families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six of a Family Killed in Fire at Home Above Grocery Store in Maharashtra
articles.excerpt: In Yedshi village, Dharashiv district, Govind and Jyoti Karande carried their son downstairs to safety, then went back into the burning home for their daughters and parents. All six who remained upstairs died.
articles.nri_angle: A Diwali-night tragedy in Maharashtra in which parents saved their son and died returning for their daughters and parents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Pollution Data Went Missing at Several Stations as Diwali Peak Hit
articles.excerpt: Readings blanked for hours on Deepavali night while PM2.5 climbed past 900 at stations that kept reporting. A Congress leader says 25 of 39 stations recorded nothing between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m.
articles.image_caption: People walk through dense smog in New Delhi on the morning after Deepavali night. Air quality data went missing at several monitoring stations as pollution peaked overnight.
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's official pollution record for Diwali night has gaps, which matters to families in Delhi and to NRIs judging conditions for travel and elderly parents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.image_caption: The Bandra-Worli Sea Link in Mumbai. The city has banned rockets and aerial firecrackers across BMC limits until November 25 after three major fires on Diwali night.
articles.nri_angle: Post-Diwali fire-safety rules for Mumbai households, including the terrace and balcony spaces where families commonly celebrate.

articles.title: Delhi Fire Calls Dip on Diwali With 214 Fire Incidents Reported Citywide

articles.image_caption: A Delhi Fire Service tender and crew are pictured on a city street. The service received 257 calls on Diwali day, down from 269 a year earlier.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families abroad who celebrated Diwali this weekend, Delhi's lower fire-call tally offers a concrete safety snapshot of how the festival passed in the capital this year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 50 Rescued From Thane High-Rise Fire as Mumbai Records 89 Diwali Fire Calls
articles.excerpt: Firefighters rescued 50 people from the Carlyle building in Thane's Raheja Garden complex on Diwali night with no casualties, while a Level-II fire hit Vidyavihar's Skyline Epitome and Mumbai logged 89 fire incidents over two days.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in Mumbai and Thane high-rises, the night's pattern — tower fires, smoke-filled floors and rocket-firework links — is the safety detail to check with housing societies before the next festival weekend.

articles.title: Delhi Wakes to Post-Diwali Smog as AQI Hits 368, 15 Areas Turn Severe
articles.excerpt: A day after Diwali, every one of Delhi's 54 monitoring stations read above 200, 15 crossed into the severe band, and PM2.5 near Akshardham peaked at more than 50 times the WHO daily limit late on Sunday night.
articles.image_caption: The sun appears as a pale disc through smog over Delhi's skyline, with buildings fading into haze. Delhi's AQI was 368 at 7 a.m. on Monday, a day after Diwali, with 15 areas in the severe category.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in Delhi, Monday's readings are the practical test of the visit-and-health advice issued before Diwali: the air stayed in the very poor to severe band across the whole city, not just in hotspots.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wisconsin Infant Dies of Measles, State's First Such Death Since 1990
articles.excerpt: The infant, in southwestern Wisconsin, was linked to an outbreak that has reached 431 cases in 13 counties — the state's highest count in more than 35 years, health officials said.
articles.image_caption: This is the skin of a patient after 3 days of measles infection; treated at the New York - Presbyterian Hospital. An infant in southwestern Wisconsin has died of measles, the first such death reported in the state since 1990, the Wisconsin Department of Health Services said on November 5; the coroner listed measles as the immediate cause of death.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Photo Credit: Content Providers(s): CDC/Dr. Heinz F. Eichenwald via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
articles.nri_angle: For families travelling between the US and India, the outbreak is a reminder to check MMR records before travel — infants too young for the standard schedule depend on the immunity of everyone around them.

articles.title: Kanpur Roof Collapse Kills Three of Family, Including Newborn Son
articles.excerpt: A woman, her 21-day-old son and her mother-in-law died after a house roof collapsed in Kanpur's Panki Padao area on Sunday morning, police said. The cause has not been officially stated.
articles.image_caption: Kanpur
articles.nri_angle: A family tragedy in Kanpur that underscores housing-safety concerns many diaspora families share for relatives in older homes in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Pens Tribute as L.K. Advani Turns 99 and Enters His 100th Year
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked Lal Krishna Advani's 99th birthday — which falls on Diwali this year — with a signed article praising the BJP co-founder's political acumen, while party leaders held a puja and havan at BJP headquarters in New Delhi.
articles.image_caption: L.K. Advani with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a recent meeting in New Delhi. Modi published a signed tribute article on November 8 as the BJP co-founder turned 99 and entered his 100th year.
articles.nri_angle: Advani shaped the BJP that much of the diaspora grew up watching from afar; his 100th year is a milestone in modern Indian political history.

articles.nri_angle: The background flydubai incident involved Indian captain Smit Machchhar, whose actions were honoured by the UAE, a detail of direct interest to Indian readers following aviation security.

articles.title: India's Clean Energy Push Could Cut Fuel Import Bill by $240 Billion, IEA Says
articles.excerpt: The IEA projects cumulative coal and gas import savings approaching $240 billion by 2030, up from more than $100 billion already saved between 2011 and 2025, if fuel prices hold near 2024-25 levels.
articles.image_caption: The graphic describes energy employment in fossil fuel and clean energy sectors, all figures used being estimates. India's clean energy push could cut its cumulative coal and natural gas import bill by nearly $240 billion by 2030, the International Energy Agency said in its India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, according to reports of the study.
articles.image_credit: Photo: International Energy Agency via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: India's renewable expansion is an energy-security and foreign-exchange story, cutting exposure to imported coal and gas prices.

articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora podcasters and comedians earn predictable income from YouTube's revenue share; Features offers them reach and invite-only deals, but no open per-view income yet.

articles.title: Debutant Aniesh Performed Every Action Scene Without a Dupe, Venky Kudumula Says
articles.excerpt: The producer says the newcomer did his own stunts in Itlu Arjuna, the mute-protagonist thriller presented by Nagarjuna and opening November 13.

articles.nri_angle: A Telugu debut built around a mute protagonist, backed by Nagarjuna and Jr NTR, is the kind of word-of-mouth release diaspora audiences track ahead of its November 13 opening.

articles.title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav Asks President to Act Against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
articles.excerpt: In a three-page letter dated November 6, Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav asked President Droupadi Murmu, as Visitor of Delhi University, for an impartial inquiry into allegedly caste-based derogatory remarks by Professor Sangeet Ragi in a televised debate.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers who studied at Delhi University or follow caste and campus politics from abroad, the case tests how India's central universities handle televised conduct by senior faculty.

articles.excerpt: Devidas (Mahadev) Takle of Deolali village in Ashti tehsil was killed on Saturday while collecting fodder for his cattle in drought-hit Maharashtra, in an attack reports link to a young male tiger camera-trapped in the area on November 2.
articles.image_caption: A Bengal tiger in a file photograph. A farmer collecting cattle fodder was mauled to death by a tiger in Maharashtra's Beed district.
articles.nri_angle: Human-wildlife conflict on farmland fringes is a recurring risk for families across Marathwada; the forest department's advisory and increased patrols are the actionable facts for anyone with family in Beed district.

articles.nri_angle: New parents in the US, including Indian-American families, face the vitamin K decision in the delivery room; the studies give them absolute-risk numbers to discuss with their care team in advance.

articles.title: Case Registered Against Former Madurai Deputy Mayor Mannan Over TVK Horse-Trading Claim
articles.excerpt: Based on Madurai Central MLA V.M.S. Mustafa's complaint, the Central Crime Branch booked former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan under the Prevention of Corruption Act and for criminal conspiracy, and picked him up for inquiry.
articles.nri_angle: The case is the latest turn in Tamil Nadu's running horse-trading row between the ruling TVK and the AIADMK-DMK opposition, a fight diaspora readers with roots in the state are following closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jharkhand High Court Quashes Cancellation of JSSC CGL Exam and Appointments
articles.excerpt: Justice Deepak Roshan set aside the government's August 18 cancellation order, restoring appointments for selected candidates while allowing the CID probe into alleged irregularities to continue.
articles.image_caption: JSSC
articles.nri_angle: Government recruitment rulings in Jharkhand affect families with members in state service, including diaspora households tracking relatives' appointments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi AQI Hits 389 as 18 Stations Record Severe Air Before Diwali
articles.excerpt: The capital's air stayed 'very poor' for a fourth day on Friday, with Rohini and IIT Delhi at 474 and forecasts warning of severe air through the Diwali weekend.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families travelling to Delhi for Diwali on November 8 will land in air forecast to stay severe to very poor through the festival weekend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India in Final-Stage Talks on Expanded BrahMos Missile Sale to Philippines
articles.excerpt: Manila is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems — nearly 60 missiles worth $700 million to $800 million, sources told Reuters — roughly double its $375 million order from 2022.
articles.image_caption: A BrahMos missile system passes along Rajpath in New Delhi during a Republic Day parade rehearsal. India is in final-stage talks to sell the Philippines about five more BrahMos systems, according to Reuters.
articles.nri_angle: A second, larger Philippine BrahMos order would mark India's emergence as a missile exporter of consequence, a shift in the country's strategic weight that diaspora readers track closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar Removes Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh Amid Wife's Complaints
articles.excerpt: The 2021-batch IPS officer has been attached to Patna headquarters in a five-officer reshuffle, after weeks of public complaints by his wife — allegations that remain untested by any inquiry.
articles.nri_angle: A district police chief's removal over a family dispute is a governance story about how personal controversies are handled inside India's police leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BJP Lost the Gokul Dairy Vote. A Cabinet Rule Change Reopened the Fight for Control
articles.excerpt: Satej Patil's panel won Maharashtra's largest milk cooperative 13-12. The cabinet then approved government-nominated voting members — and the opposition calls it a stolen mandate.
articles.nri_angle: Cooperative boards decide milk prices and procurement for lakh of farmers; the fight over Gokul is a live test of how far a state government can go after losing a cooperative election.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
